name: dockerhub
description: Reads public Docker Hub repositories and image tags for a configured target namespace; an optional Personal Access Token authenticates as a separately configured Docker Hub username. It also manages access tokens, organizations, groups/teams, invites, audit logs, and repositories via the Docker Hub API.

risk.read: external Docker Hub API read of public repository/tag data, and, when authenticated, account-scoped access-token/org/group/invite/audit-log metadata
risk.approval: reverse ETL mutations (repository, access-token, group, invite, org member/settings writes) require plan, preview, explicit approval, and execute; destructive actions require typed destructive confirmation

conformance.reason: custom-auth-optional (mode:custom dockerhub AuthHook gated by when: secrets.docker_pat, falling back to mode:none for unauthenticated public reads) -- conformance's runtimeConfigForEngine synthesizes a non-empty value for every x-secret property unconditionally, so the docker_pat when-gate always evaluates true under conformance and every dynamic check (even the 4 pre-existing public-read streams) is forced onto the custom-hook path, which then fails closed on the synthetic non-URL base_url value; there is no synthetic-config shape that can exercise both the authenticated and unauthenticated branches faithfully. The AuthHook's own login-exchange behavior (request shape, JWT-exp-driven caching/refresh, error handling, secret redaction) is proven by internal/connectors/hooks/dockerhub/hooks_test.go against a real httptest.Server, and the 4 pre-existing public-read stream fixtures under fixtures/streams/** are unchanged from before this phase and were passing dynamic conformance prior to the auth hook's addition.
